## Welcome 

Good public health decisions depend on good data.

The **St Helena Public Health Data Skills Programme** is a practical learning programme designed to help build the skills needed to collect, manage, analyse, and interpret health data responsibly.

This is not a traditional short course. It is a **mentored learning programme built around real public health questions**, realistic datasets, and practical analytical work.

Our aim is straightforward:

> To help develop confident, careful, and useful public health data practice in St Helena.

## Who this learning programme is for

The learning materials are designed to support several different roles within the health system.

- **Data staff** involved in data entry, management, and quality assurance  
- **Epidemiology or research trainees** working with health data  
- **Data producers**, including clinicians and programme staff  
- **Evidence consumers**, such as managers and decision-makers

Not everyone needs every module. The programme is modular so that people can focus on the material most relevant to their role. We can help you decide which modules are most relevant to your work.

## How the learning works

The programme is designed for a small health system where people already have busy roles.

Most learning happens **asynchronously**.

Participants work through short modules at their own pace and then meet periodically to discuss progress, ask questions, and review analytical work.

A typical learning cycle could look like this:

1. read the module overview  
2. work through the key concepts  
3. complete a practical exercise  
4. produce a short analytical output  
5. review the work during a mentoring discussion

We hope that in this way, learning happens **through doing**.

## What the programme focuses on

The modules focus on the practical work required to generate useful public health intelligence.

Topics include:

- responsible handling of health data  
- understanding how datasets are built and managed  
- checking and improving data quality  
- analysing population health data  
- interpreting epidemiological results carefully  
- communicating findings clearly  
- building reproducible analytical workflows

The emphasis is on **good judgement and practical usefulness**, not just technical skill.

## Why this matters for St Helena

In small populations, good data practice matters even more.

Small numbers can make confidentiality more sensitive.  
Limited staff and temporary visiting staff make documentation and reproducibility essential.  
Scarce resources mean analysis must be clear, careful, and directly relevant to real decisions.

Building strong data practice is therefore an important part of strengthening the health system.

## A living learning resource

This learning hub will grow gradually.

The earlier modules will be developed in full from the start. Others will be added as new needs arise and as local experience develops.

The goal is not to create a fixed manual. The goal is to build a **useful, evolving resource that supports public health data capability in St Helena**.
